newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies to see light rains over weekend.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies to see light rains over weekend.

text.p: Canada's Prairie grainbelt on Friday was forecast to see light scattered showers through the weekend, Environment Canada said.
"We're looking at instability, showers over the next 48 hours for the Prairies with normal to a few degrees above normal temperatures," Environment Canada meteorologist Phil Wright said.
The normal high at this time of year is 25 Celsius (77 F).
Much of western Canada's 21.955 million acres of wheat entered the heading stage, the stage in growth where the grain needs moisture the most.
Provincial grain analysts on Thursday forecast Prairie wheat output to match or exceed the five year average.

The latest production estimate issued by the International Grains Institute on Thursday, however, cut Canada's output outlook to 25.5 million tonnes from 27 million due to "a major shift to canola, flaxseed and other more profitable crops."
Western Canadian wheat area was down 10 percent compared to the prior year and canola acreage was projected to rise 38 percent in Statistics Canada's June 27 estimate.
